vectors.note: REFERENCE DEFECT. For an all-zero payload the Base58 string is all '1', and base58_decode then reaches base58.c:144 with size = 1 and low = 2, calling memcpy with a length of (size_t)(-1). Reproduced under lldb; it faults every time. The NULL length-probe on the same input returns 21 for a 22-byte payload -- one short -- so even a caller that sizes its buffer from the probe is already wrong before the memcpy. base58_encode has the matching probe defect (all-zero 20-byte input probes 19, writes 20 characters plus a NUL) but does not fault. An all-zero tag is a reachable value, so a Rust implementation must decode this correctly and must not reproduce either the short probe or the fault.
vectors.falsifies: survey §2: base58_decode's length probe is reliable for all inputs
vectors.correct_out_expected: 22 zero bytes -- the C cannot be asked for this value, so it is stated as the requirement rather than emitted as a reference output

vectors.note: CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION CHECK. A bare 2144-byte WOTS+ public key of 0x42 bytes, taken from the TypeScript package's own test for addrFromWots. Unlike every C4-A* vector there is no key generation behind this input, so it exercises addr_from_wots on bytes the reference did not itself produce. The expected address is the literal that test asserts; group_c_crosscheck.json carries the value obtained by running that TypeScript, which is the stronger form.

crc16_base58_corpus.note: tag[i] = the first 20 bytes of sha256(ull_to_bytes(i, 8)). Both helpers are reference functions, so even the inputs are not hand-rolled. crc16 and base58 are the reference's outputs.
